messages.title: End
segments: There was once a place where nothing grew. Only water, bones, and things nobody came back for. He walked until the rooms began to repeat.
A word, a joke, an olive, a memory, he kept searching for the things waiting at the end...
... but there was no door, no answer, no one waiting, only the swamp, only the dead.
And behind him, a small fire still burning ... He finally understood.
Nothing had been waiting for him at the end. Everything had been waiting for him along the way. So he stopped searching.
And listened to the fire. It was the only thing in the dungeon that was still alive.

messages.title: Goblin
segments: You came all this way for her.
Don’t bother lying.
I’ve seen that look before.
You remember the little things, don’t you? The things nobody else would remember.
The stupid jokes. The strange names. The things she liked because you liked them.
That’s how you know it was real. (looks toward the empty throne room.)
Not because it lasted.
Because you still remember.
That’s the cruel part. You can lose someone... and keep everything they left inside you.
So tell me. What exactly are you hoping to find at the end of this place? Her?
Or the version of you that existed when she was here?
But you can’t go back. You can only remember. I suppose that’s why I built this place.
A kingdom full of things that stayed.
People are much harder to keep.

messages.title: Skeleton
segments: Oh. You.
I was hoping you wouldn’t come this far.
Not because you’re dangerous. You just look like the sort of person who is going to ask questions.
You: What are you doing here?
That’s a very good question.
Unfortunately, I’ve been trying to remember the answer for quite some time.
I think I was looking for something.
Or someone.
At some point I stopped being sure which one. (Looking around ...)
Then again, perhaps I was only looking for a way out. I don’t remember that either.

messages.title: What were you looking for
segments: I told you. Something.
Very useful, I know.
I remember walking for a long time. There were doors, rooms, corridors…
Every time I found something, I thought it was the thing I had come for.
You: And was it?
No. Usually it was a chair. Or a rusty sword. Once I walked three rooms because I thought I smelled bread. It was a rat.
I don’t even remember what I was hoping to find anymore. That’s the part that bothers me. Not that I failed. That I can’t remember what winning would have looked like.

messages.title: Someone
segments: Did I?
You: Yes.
Hmph.
Then I suppose I meant someone.
There was someone. I remember that much. I remember wanting to find them.
I remember thinking that if I just kept walking, eventually I’d reach them.
Look at me. What do you think? I don’t even remember their face anymore.
But I remember that I missed them. Funny thing, memory. Sometimes it takes the person and leaves you with the feeling.

messages.title: Why are you still here
segments: Because apparently I have terrible judgment.
I could have left. Probably. I think there was a way out somewhere behind me.
I have been dead for a while. You’ll have to forgive me if my memory isn’t perfect. The strange thing is, I remember wanting to leave.
I just don’t remember why I stayed. Maybe I thought they would come looking for me. Or maybe I was afraid that if I left, they wouldn’t know where to find me.

messages.title: Who are you?
segments: You: Who are you ?
Nobody important
That’s usually what people ask when they’ve reached the end of somewhere.
They expect a king. A demon. A treasure. Something with enough teeth to make the journey feel worthwhile. Instead, you got me. Terrible ending, isn’t it?

messages.title: What is this place ?
segments: The part you weren’t supposed to reach.
The rooms behind the rooms.
The things left behind after memories have eaten everything useful.
You called it a dungeon because that made it easier to walk through.
People like names.
Names make terrible things feel organized.

messages.title: Why are you here ?
segments: Because somebody has to clean up.
You: Clean up what?
Time.
Memory.
Regret.
All the little pieces people refuse to throw away.
Mostly memory. Memory is disgusting. It never knows when to die.

messages.title: The Vampires of Time
segments: You: What do you mean by time?
Time is hungry.
It eats everything.
Faces.
Voices.
Places.
The exact sound someone made when they laughed.
The things you thought you’d never forget.
Eventually, time comes for all of it.
But there are things that refuse to be eaten.
You: Like what?
Memories.
Little parasites. They hide inside you and wait. Then, years later, something stupid happens. An olive. A stupid joke. A smell. A place. And suddenly they've awake
That’s when the vampires of time have already lost.

messages.title: Why does everything remind me of her?
segments: Because you let her in.
You: What does that mean?
You gave ordinary things meaning.
You let them become yours.
Then hers.
Then both.
Now you can’t tell where one ends and the other begins.
That’s the price.
You: What price?
Caring. You people always want the good part. The laughing. The stupid little things. The feeling that someone somewhere understands you. Nobody tells you about the fucking archaeology afterward.

messages.title: Is she here?
segments: That’s not the right question.
You: Then what is?
Why are you still looking? You’ve been carrying her through this entire place.
Every room. Every stupid little object. Every word you remembered.
And you still came looking for her. You really are terrible at letting things stay where they happened.

messages.title: He came here
segments: No
You brought him here.
He walks because you tell him where to go.
He opens the doors because you make him curious.
He picks up the little things because you want to know what they mean.
You thought you were searching for her.
You’ve been searching through him.
That’s rather cruel.
Making someone walk through everything you remember.

messages.title: I miss her.
segments: I know.
You: How?
You built a fucking dungeon about it.
What else was I supposed to think?
You: I don’t know what to do with it.
Nothing.
You don’t have to solve missing someone. You don’t have to defeat it. You don’t have to turn it into something beautiful. Sometimes you just miss them.
And it hurts. Then it hurts less. Then one day something reminds you again. And it hurts a little. That’s memory. It doesn’t need your permission.

messages.title: Then why did I come here?
segments: Because you wanted an ending.
You: Isn’t there one?
Look around.
This is what endings look like.
Unremarkable.
A little ugly. Mostly empty. No Music. No grand revelation. Just the thing you were  carrying… and the moment you finally realize you’re still carrying it.

messages.title: End
segments: You: What am I supposed to do now?
You?
Nothing.
For once, stop making him walk. You’ve been looking for her in every room.
In the books. In the fire. In the little things. In the things you almost forgot. You found her everywhere.
Except where you wanted her to be. That’s the part you hate. Not that she disappeared. That she didn’t disappear completely.
If she had…
…this place wouldn’t exist.
Go. Take him with you. You've kept him here long enough.
And stop looking behind you. There is nothing there.
Except everything you remember.
